evidence.quote: I don't think I'm going to move off it. We do this one site at a time.
No parallel cutovers, not even for the two small ones.

observations.why: Tanya states an unmovable operational stance and rules out parallel cutovers firmly.

evidence.quote: I still think it's the wrong trade.

observations.why: Tanya defends her position against Xavier's test using comparative risk reasoning.

evidence.quote: the desk supervisor's pain is a rota problem, which is solvable.

observations.why: Tina offers a structured defense supporting Tanya's stance.

evidence.quote: Right. So: one at a time, with a soak.

observations.why: Tanya ratifies the one-at-a-time sequencing decision.

evidence.quote: The soak is two full weeks. That's the Dockside number, and I'd hold us to it.

observations.why: Tina strongly proposes and stakes out a two-week duration requirement.

evidence.quote: Two weeks gives you the flattening plus a few days to actually look at what flattened.

observations.why: Tina provides empirical defense from the spring pilot curve.

evidence.quote: That's the reasoning I wanted on the record. Two weeks, from the Dockside exception curve.

observations.why: Tanya puts the two-week duration on the official record, ratifying it.

evidence.quote: I'd rather hold two weeks and shorten it with evidence than hold one week and discover we needed two.

observations.why: Tina defends the conservatism of the duration estimate.

evidence.quote: Not "should", not "where possible" — reporting does not touch the live system during a cutover window, full stop.

observations.why: Xavier proposes an absolute operational rule with strict boundaries.

evidence.quote: My argument is that a four-minute-stale number is fine and an outage is not.

observations.why: Xavier frames his trade-off argument ready to defend it.

evidence.quote: Then that's the rule. Reporting reads come off the replica during cutover.
write it into the runbook as a rule and not as guidance

observations.why: Tanya formally adopts the rule and directs it to be written into the runbook as binding.

evidence.quote: The vendor stays the system of record for reference data until the last site is live.
and we take ownership on the day Clyde goes green and not a day earlier.

observations.why: Xavier outlines his recommended position on reference data ownership.

evidence.quote: Keeping one source of truth through the whole programme is worth more than getting ownership early.

observations.why: Xavier articulates the rationale behind delaying system-of-record ownership.

evidence.quote: I agree with that, and I'd add: it also means the vendor can't tell the steering group that their reference data was fine and ours broke it.

observations.why: Tanya seconds the claim and adds defensive rationale.

evidence.quote: So Thursday I'm telling them: one site at a time, two-week soak between sites, reporting off the replica during cutover, vendor holds reference data until Clyde is green.

observations.why: Tanya summarizes the four ratified decisions to take to the steering group.
